title: fix: separate community health from service KPI
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Excludes `model_provider_used = community` from the regular service-health pipe
- Keeps community availability in its existing dedicated KPI
- Clarifies the KPI tooltips and adds mutual-exclusion regression coverage

Tests: `npm test -- --run test/kpis.test.js`; `npm run build`; Tinybird staging `deployment create --check --no-allow-destructive-operations`

gist.headline: Two hives, two health checks
gist.blurb: Community availability now gets its own little garden bed instead of being counted in the main service-weather report. The numbers have stopped borrowing each other's umbrellas.
gist.summary: Weekly health reporting now excludes requests with `model_provider_used = community` from the regular service-health pipeline while retaining community availability in its dedicated KPI, with clarified tooltips and regression coverage.
gist.impact: Operators and community members get cleaner, mutually exclusive service and community availability metrics, making each health signal easier to interpret.
gist.visual_concept: Depict two neighboring but separate garden health stations: one for the main service hive and one for the community garden, each with its own clear gauge. Polli acts as a careful gardener holding a clipboard and placing community flowers into their dedicated plot, while a friendly CRT monitor robot reads two distinct green status displays.
gist.image_prompt: A cozy pixel art observability garden with two clearly separate lime green (#ecf874) health gauges: a main service hive gauge and a community flower-bed gauge, both glowing calmly. Polli, the cute yellow-and-brown striped bee with pink cheek blush, light blue wings, and a tiny gardener visor, carefully sorts flowers into the community plot while a chunky CRT monitor robot checks the separate readouts; code-plants and soft pastel vines surround them. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, subtle pixel-font labels: "SERVICE" and "COMMUNITY", nostalgic but beautiful.
